The function is determined by 8 values, and no fewer suffice.

**Structure of f.** The first equation says f(a+1, b, c) − 2f(a, b, c) + f(a−1, b, c) = 0. So for fixed b and c, f is an affine function of a. The same holds in b and in c.

Write f(a, b, c) = p(b, c) + a·q(b, c). Both p(b, c) = f(0, b, c) and q(b, c) = f(1, b, c) − f(0, b, c) inherit the second-difference condition in b and in c, because those conditions are linear and commute with the shift in a. So p and q are each affine in b and in c. Repeating the argument on b and then on c gives

f(a, b, c) = Σ over i, j, k ∈ {0, 1} of c_{ijk} · aⁱ bʲ cᵏ.

This is a multilinear polynomial. The set of all such f is a real vector space of dimension 8, and every such polynomial satisfies all three equations.

**Lower bound.** The space of valid f has dimension 8. Evaluation at n points is a linear map from this space to ℝⁿ, and it can be injective only if n ≥ 8. So at least 8 evaluations are needed.

**Upper bound.** The 8 points of {0, 1}³ suffice. Given f on these points, f(a, 0, 0) is affine in a and is fixed by its values at a = 0 and a = 1, so it is known for all a. Extending in b and then in c the same way determines f everywhere.

The minimum is 8.

ANSWER: 8
